1	// ★ THE DENOMINATOR, EXTRACTED SO IT CAN BE RUN INSTEAD OF GREPPED.
2	//
3	// `lspVerifiedPct` was computed inline in health.js, so the only way to guard it was to
4	// assert regexes over that file — eight of them, all spelling. the field test rates this
5	// denominator among the fields they ACTUALLY USED (they checked the 833/1599 arithmetic
6	// against it), which makes a test that cannot fail on a wrong number the worst kind to
7	// have here.
8	//
9	// Pulling it out is a small refactor with a large consequence: the invariant becomes
10	// checkable by calling it with rows and comparing integers.
11	//
12	// THE INVARIANTS, each of which was a real defect at some point:
13	//
14	//  1. DIVIDE BY THE VERIFIABLE SUBSET, NOT BY EVERY CALLS EDGE. Dividing by all calls
15	//     reported 12% on a repo where every verifiable edge was verified — a number that
16	//     read as a coverage failure and was an accounting one.
17	//  2. OUT-OF-SCOPE EDGES NEVER ENTER, AND NEVER MIGRATE IN. An edge outside the tracked
18	//     corpus is not verifiable debt; if a backend for its language later lands, it must
19	//     not silently appear in the denominator and drop the percentage.
20	//  3. UNVERIFIABLE-BY-CONSTRUCTION IS NOT UNVERIFIED-BY-OMISSION. A JS edge in a C++-only
21	//     collection was never going to be verified. Counting it as a miss blames the tool
22	//     for a language it does not claim.
23	//  4. UNKNOWN SCOPE ≠ EVERYTHING IN SCOPE. If the tracked-file list cannot be read, the
24	//     honest answer is that scope is unknown — not that every edge is in it.
25	
26	// Languages an LSP backend in this server can actually verify. Anything else is
27	// unverifiable by construction.
28	export const LSP_VERIFIABLE_LANGUAGES = new Set(['cpp', 'c', 'cxx', 'cc', 'h', 'hpp']);
29	
30	/**
31	 * @param {Array<{lang: string, c: number, inScope?: boolean}>} langScopeRows
32	 *        one row per (language, scope) bucket with a count.
33	 * @param {number} verified  edges actually verified by an LSP backend.
34	 * @returns {{
35	 *   verifiable: number, verified: number, pct: number,
36	 *   denominator: string,
37	 *   outOfScope: number,
38	 *   unverifiable: Array<{reason: string, lang: string, count: number}>
39	 * }}
40	 */
41	export function computeCoverage(langScopeRows = [], verified = 0) {
42	  const outOfScopeRows = langScopeRows.filter((r) => r.inScope === false);
43	  const inScopeRows = langScopeRows.filter((r) => r.inScope !== false);
44	
45	  const verifiable = inScopeRows
46	    .filter((r) => LSP_VERIFIABLE_LANGUAGES.has(r.lang))
47	    .reduce((a, r) => a + r.c, 0);
48	
49	  const unverifiable = inScopeRows
50	    .filter((r) => !LSP_VERIFIABLE_LANGUAGES.has(r.lang))
51	    .map((r) => ({ reason: 'non_cpp_language', lang: r.lang, count: r.c }));
52	
53	  return {
54	    verifiable,
55	    verified,
56	    // Guard the divide: a zero denominator reports 0, never NaN or Infinity — a NaN
57	    // percentage renders as a plausible-looking blank rather than as an error.
58	    pct: verifiable > 0 ? Math.round((verified / verifiable) * 100) : 0,
59	    // The denominator names its own population. This is the `basis` pattern that §4 of
60	    // the plan generalises from — a ratio that travels without its denominator is how
61	    // two correct numbers produce a wrong comparison.
62	    denominator: 'verifiable_and_in_scope_calls',
63	    outOfScope: outOfScopeRows.reduce((a, r) => a + r.c, 0),
64	    unverifiable,
65	  };
66	}
67

1413	  // A stored collection with ZERO materialized [lsp✓] edges is the silent
1414	  // failure mode that makes this tool look useless: every caller query falls back
1415	  // to the heuristic layer, so nothing can attest exhaustiveness, and nothing
1416	  // says why. Measured on a real project: 0 of 17544 CALLS verified after a
1417	  // reindex moved HEAD past the collection. One command fixes it.
1418	  if (codeIntel?.available) {

1424	        codeIntel.lspVerifiedEdges = verified;
1425	        // ⛔ THE FILE COUNT IS A DIFFERENT POPULATION FROM THE EDGE COUNT, and the coverage warning
1426	        // was answering an EDGES question with a RECORDS number for want of it. `[lsp✓]` renders
1427	        // from `edges.provenance` alone (renderer.js, trace.js), so the files carrying a verified
1428	        // edge are the only files the marker can ever appear on. Read from the SAME handle at the
1429	        // SAME instant as `verified` above — a second open is a second graph.
1430	        //
1431	        // ⚠ NULL WOULD BE A LIE HERE AND ZERO WOULD NOT: this block runs only when a collection is
1432	        // available, and the COUNT cannot fail without the query beside it failing too, in which
1433	        // case the catch below leaves the field undefined and the sentence says UNKNOWN.
1434	        codeIntel.lspVerifiedFiles = db2.get(
1435	          "SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT source_file) AS c FROM edges WHERE provenance = 'LSP_VERIFIED'",
1436	        ).c ?? 0;
1437	
1438	        // ★ ATTACK EIGHT — THE DENOMINATOR WAS CONTAMINATED WITH EDGES THAT ARE
1439	        //   UNVERIFIABLE IN PRINCIPLE.
1440	        //
1441	        // the field test, on the headline coverage number I had been quoting to him
1442	        // since day one and that neither of us had ever opened up. The denominator
1443	        // was every CALLS edge, unrestricted. This repo's graph contains GLSL and
1444	        // Python: clangd cannot verify a single one of those edges — not because
1445	        // the index is cold, but because they are not C++ and were never in
1446	        // compile_commands.json.
1447	        //
1448	        // Measured here: 15530 CALLS = 12830 cpp + 1458 glsl + 1242 python. So
1449	        // 17.4% of the denominator was unverifiable BY CONSTRUCTION, and the
1450	        // number could never approach 100 however good collection got. Worse, its
1451	        // MOVEMENT was uninterpretable: a rise could mean better verification, or
1452	        // merely fewer shader edges after a refactor.
1453	        //
1454	        // And it broke the word `floor`, which is load-bearing here. A floor
1455	        // implies the true value is above it and reachable. A ratio over a
1456	        // contaminated denominator is not a floor of anything — it is a different
1457	        // quantity wearing a coverage label.
1458	        //
1459	        // His generalization of tonight's other fix is exact: AN EDGE NOBODY COULD
1460	        // HAVE VERIFIED IS NOT AN EDGE THAT FAILED VERIFICATION. Same shape as the
1461	        // other five instances — a percentage stood in for coverage while the real
1462	        // thing, the verifiable subset, was computable from data already in hand.
1463	        // ★ ATTACK NINE — SCOPE AND VERIFIABILITY ARE ORTHOGONAL, AND THE
1464	        //   LANGUAGE-ONLY MODEL CONFLATED THEM.
1465	        //
1466	        // the field test caught this in the attack-eight FIX, one commit old. Making
1467	        // verifiability a language set means that when a Python backend lands,
1468	        // every Python call edge reclassifies from `unverifiable` to `verifiable`
1469	        // and enters the denominator as legitimate coverage debt — regardless of
1470	        // whether those files are part of the project at all.
1471	        //
1472	        // The two classes he named are both real and were indistinguishable:
1473	        //   (in-scope, unverifiable)  — GLSL under engine/voxel/shaders: real code
1474	        //                               you cannot check yet. Belongs in the debt.
1475	        //   (out-of-scope, verifiable) — vendored C++: you COULD check it and must
1476	        //                               never count it.
1477	        //
1478	        // ★ AND THE SCOPE PREDICATE ITSELF MUST NOT BE A STAND-IN. A path-prefix
1479	        // guess (engine/|game/|tests/) is exactly the failure this session named
1480	        // six times: it would have silently excluded tools/ and the repo-root
1481	        // scripts, which ARE first-party. The real signal is git tracking — a file
1482	        // the project version-controls is a file the project owns — and it is one
1483	        // command away. Vendored trees, build outputs and stale worktrees are all
1484	        // untracked by construction, so this is a stronger predicate than any
1485	        // prefix list AND it needs no maintenance.
1486	        const trackedFiles = (() => {
1487	          try {
1488	            const out = execFileSync('git', ['ls-files'], {
1489	              cwd: repoRoot, encoding: 'utf8', stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'ignore'],
1490	              windowsHide: true, maxBuffer: 64 * 1024 * 1024,

content.text:
`graph_health`'s coverage percentage divided two different populations, and I've fixed it. The unit tests pass, but I haven't run any wider test run to completion, and I haven't re-run `graph_health` on a real graph.

**Cause.** In `health.js` the denominator was verifiable, in-scope `CALLS` edges only (C/C++ files tracked by git). The numerator was `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM edges WHERE provenance = 'LSP_VERIFIED'`. That counts every verified edge of any relation, language and scope. So 949 verified edges sat over 19 in-scope C++ calls, which gave 4995%. I haven't opened your graph, so I haven't confirmed which kind of edge made up the extra 930. Any of out-of-scope vendored C++, non-`CALLS` relations or non-C++ edges would produce this.

**Fix.**
- `mcp/stdio/query/verbs/health.js`: one bucketing helper now builds both sides of the ratio. It takes `CALLS` edges grouped by source language and tracked scope, once for all calls and once for `LSP_VERIFIED` calls only.
- `mcp/stdio/query/coverage-denominator.js`: `computeCoverage` now takes the verified rows and applies the same scope and language filter as the denominator. The numerator is a subset of the denominator, so the percentage can't go above 100.
- The raw `lspVerifiedEdges` field and the `verified === 0` warning still use the all-edges count. I left them alone because they report a different quantity.

**Tests.** I added a regression for the 949-over-19 shape. It uses 12 verified in-scope C++ calls over 19, plus 930 out-of-scope and 7 Python verified calls, and expects 63%. I also added a subset-never-exceeds-100% test and converted the existing tests to the new signature. All 9 pass. I stashed the fix and re-ran: 4 of the 9 fail on the old code (all converted to the new signature), so the tests do catch this bug.

**Not run yet.** A run of `suite-composition` and the health-verb tests is still going in the background. Nothing exercises the real SQL path in `health.js` end to end. The new query is a copy of the existing denominator query plus one `AND` clause. I haven't committed anything.
